title: Sealed VPC: Network & Upgrade Acceptance Contract for Private Deployments
creator: Anika Patel
description: Purpose: Define a minimal, testable acceptance contract for Private/VPC deployments operating with zero or highly restricted egress ("sealed"/air‑gapped) that covers networking prerequisites, encrypted artifact delivery, upgrade sequencing, and operator rollback guarantees. Scope: networking ACLs and routing rules, artifact distribution strategy (signed bundles, mirror endpoints), upgrade orchestration steps, preflight/health checks, and observability for canary and full rollouts. Out of scope: on‑prem hardware procurement, region-level networking topologies, and tenant onboarding UX. Motivation: Multiple recent customer engagements require predictable, auditable upgrade behavior in environments that disallow outbound connections except to allowed mirrors or signed USB transfer. Current ambiguity in acceptance criteria causes lengthy SRE handoffs and blocked upgrades. This PRD captures explicit gates and fallbacks so Dedicated/Private teams and customers can validate readiness before an upgrade window.
acceptance_criteria: Network posture: The cluster can be validated to operate with only the allowed egress endpoints using a deterministic checklist; validation scripts return success/failed with explicit failing rule IDs.
Signed artifact delivery: All image/artifact bundles used in private upgrades must be signed. The operator verifies signature against an on‑cluster pinned root key before applying any changes.
Mirror bootstrap: For customers using mirror endpoints, the operator supports staged mirroring: initial metadata sync, blob sync, and integrity verification steps with resumable transfer semantics.
Checksum reconciliation: The upgrade flow performs manifest checksum comparison post‑fetch and before unpack; mismatch triggers automatic rollback to preupgrade manifest and emits an incident log.

KMS rotation path (airgapped): Provide an offline KMS rotation procedure (documented playbook) that includes local key wrapping, operator handshake, and acceptance validation; testable in a customer lab.

Canary sequencing: A canary upgrade mode must run against a pinned subset of nodes with traffic diversion controlled by the Console or operator flag; metrics must be collected for 30 minutes minimum before rollout continues or aborts.

Observability: Upgrade events, artifact checksums, and network validation results are emitted to the local audit log with a minimum 90‑day retention option; telemetry must be exportable via SFTP or mirror pull for customers.

Rollback guarantee: If any non‑transient preflight or canary check fails, the operator must automatically revert to the prior release within configured SLA (default 15 minutes) and mark the rollout as failed with root cause annotation.
Operator isolation: The operator must not attempt outbound connections to unknown hosts; any outbound DNS/HTTP attempts are blocked and flagged as security exceptions in preflight.

Manual offline artifact option: Customers can provide a signed artifact bundle via removable media; the operator validates signatures and checksums and transitions to the same upgrade flow as mirror deliveries.
Test harness: Provide an integration test harness (local Vagrant/VM or k3s recipe) that simulates sealed network conditions and validates the complete upgrade contract end‑to‑end.
Acceptable performance: Under sealed mode, upgrade total duration for a medium cluster (10 nodes) must not exceed 3x the hosted upgrade baseline; documented test results required in PRD.
Compliance evidence: Generate a machine‑readable upgrade report containing artifacts, checksums, applied manifests, and operator decisions suitable for customer audit ingestion.
Fallback notification: If automatic rollback occurs, the operator opens an incident with prepopulated runbook links and a bifurcated remediation path (retry vs. manual intervention).
Security signoff: Security team must complete the offline artifact threat model and approve the playbook before GA trade release is scheduled.
